insights.question: How has French-English bilingualism changed in Canada over time?
insights.text: English–French bilingualism in Canada increased from 12.3% in 1951 to 18.0% in 2021 (change of +5.6 percentage points).

insights.question: How has bilingualism changed since 2001?
insights.text: Between 2001 and 2021, the Canadian bilingualism rate changed from 17.6% to 18.0% (+0.3 pp).

insights.question: Which provinces have the highest levels of French-English bilingualism?
insights.text: Among provinces, Quebec had the highest English–French bilingualism rate in 2021 at 46.4%.

insights.question: How does French usage differ geographically?
insights.text: In 2021, English–French bilingualism was 46.4% in Quebec and 9.5% in Canada outside Quebec. These are different language regimes; the gap is descriptive, not a ranking of quality.

insights.question: Where is French most commonly used at home?
insights.text: In 2021, Quebec had the highest share of people speaking French most often at home among provinces (79.1%).

insights.question: Where is French most commonly used in the workplace?
insights.text: In Canada (2021 home language; 2021 workplace), French spoken most often at home was 19.8% while French used most often at work was 19.3%. Home and workplace language measure different populations and should not be treated as the same behaviour.

insights.question: How does French knowledge vary among newcomers?
insights.text: In 2021, among immigrants in Canada, 16.4% could converse in French (French only or English and French). This is a Census knowledge measure, not a sample of learners in this app.

insights.question: How does French knowledge vary among newcomers?
insights.text: In 2021, among immigrants in Canada outside Quebec, 5.5% could converse in French (French only or English and French). This is a Census knowledge measure, not a sample of learners in this app.

insights.question: How does French knowledge vary among newcomers?
insights.text: In 2021, among immigrants in Quebec, 80.5% could converse in French (French only or English and French). This is a Census knowledge measure, not a sample of learners in this app.
